section_summary: This section examines Japan’s gold production, purchase premiums, restrictions, reserves, exports, and foreign trade from late 1939 through 1940. It then follows 1941 inquiries into Japanese gold shipments to Brazil and Peru, including a State Department survey of diplomatic missions in Central and South America.

subfiles.title: Gold premium press clippings
subfiles.from: Japan Chronicle; Mitsubishi Economic Research Bureau; Osaka Mainichi; Japan Times
subfiles.about: Clippings describe Japanese and Manchukuo premiums intended to increase newly mined gold output.
subfiles.summary: The clippings explain production premiums, compare official purchase prices with dollar gold prices, and describe a similar premium system in Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Attachment No. 5: New Gold Restrictions for 1940
subfiles.about: A cover sheet identifies an attachment on new gold restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet for the following clipping.

subfiles.title: Gold Restrictions: Revised Rules to Go Into Force on January 1st
subfiles.about: Japan expands controls on the use and transfer of gold from January 1940.
subfiles.summary: The revised rules cover additional gold forms and require permission for sales and transfers.

subfiles.title: Attachment No. 6: Excess of Imports Over Exports in Japan's Foreign Trade
subfiles.about: A cover sheet identifies a foreign trade table.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet for the following table.

subfiles.title: Japan's Excess of Imports Over Exports in 1939
subfiles.about: A table separates Japan's January–October 1939 trade with the yen bloc from other trade.
subfiles.summary: Despite an overall export surplus, trade outside the yen bloc shows an import excess of ¥461,919,546.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference file note: Japanese gold at end of 1939
subfiles.about: The sheet points to a memorandum filed elsewhere on Japanese gold at the end of 1939.
subfiles.summary: References memorandum 894.51/656.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Bank of Japan gold reserve figures
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: The memorandum compares conflicting published Bank of Japan reserve figures with an earlier estimate.
subfiles.summary: Reports from Kobe and Tokyo conflict over whether the reserve fell from roughly ¥501 million to ¥369.78 million. The lower figure closely matches the writer's estimate after a late December gold shipment.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding memoranda on Japanese gold and foreign exchange
subfiles.about: Feis forwards four memoranda about Japanese gold and foreign exchange assets.
subfiles.summary: Forwards four memoranda to Wiley at the Treasury Department.

subfiles.title: Japan's Decreasing Gold Exports
subfiles.from: L. H. Gourley, American consul at Kobe
subfiles.about: The report assesses falling Japanese gold exports, production, private collections, official reserves, and note circulation.
subfiles.summary: Gold exports in the first half of 1940 were far below recent annual levels. Gourley considers whether newly mined gold could cover exports, doubts that voluntary private collections can supply much more, and examines conflicting Bank of Japan reserve reports. The report notes that official secrecy prevents a firm reserve estimate.

subfiles.title: Gold Exports from Japan to United States
subfiles.about: The attachment tabulates monthly 1940 shipments and annual Japanese gold exports to the United States since 1937.
subfiles.summary: Consular figures record 818,187 troy ounces exported through July 16, 1940, and 18.46 million ounces from 1937 through that date.

subfiles.title: Japan's Gold Position
subfiles.about: An embassy analysis estimates Japanese gold stocks and relates gold shipments to foreign trade and U.S. assets.
subfiles.summary: The analysis estimates 73,777 kilograms of gold on hand on November 1, 1940, using uncertain production, collection, consumption, and export figures. It calculates a merchandise and gold debit balance and considers how much Japan may have drawn on commercial assets in the United States. It projects continued import needs and discusses the effect of U.S. export restrictions.

subfiles.title: Gold Compulsory Purchase Law: Commercial Attaché report
subfiles.about: The report introduces translations of Japan's compulsory gold purchase ordinance and related notifications.
subfiles.summary: Williams describes Japan's efforts to collect private gold and explains the ordinance, designated articles and depositories, and ¥3.85-per-gram purchase price.

subfiles.title: Gold Compulsory Purchase Law, Finance Ministry Ordinance No. 73
subfiles.about: The ordinance authorizes compulsory sale of specified gold and gold articles, with exemptions and procedures.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance empowers the Finance Minister to order sales of gold, gold coins, and gold articles. It provides exemptions or permission procedures for industrial, medical, research, artistic, and historic uses; restricts private transactions; and permits reporting and inspections.

subfiles.title: Finance Ministry Notification No. 344
subfiles.about: The notification lists gold articles subject to the compulsory purchase rules.
subfiles.summary: Lists jewelry, personal effects, utensils, furnishings, sword fittings, stationery, and coins.

subfiles.title: Finance Ministry Notification No. 345
subfiles.about: The notification names institutions authorized under the compulsory purchase law.
subfiles.summary: Names the Bank of Japan and two Tokyo associations.

subfiles.title: Finance Ministry Notification No. 346
subfiles.about: The notification sets the compulsory purchase valuation for gold alloys and articles.
subfiles.summary: Sets the price at ¥3.85 per gram of pure gold content.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1006 from Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.from: Caffery, American Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: The Yokohama Specie Bank proposes placing gold with the Bank of Brazil for safekeeping.
subfiles.summary: Brazil's Director of Exchange intends to decline the proposal.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Rio de Janeiro telegram 1006
subfiles.about: A paraphrase reports the proposed Japanese gold transfer to the Bank of Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Restates Brazil's intended refusal.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Rio de Janeiro telegram to Treasury
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards six copies of the paraphrased Rio de Janeiro telegram.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the report on the proposed Bank of Brazil deposit.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1696 from Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew reports two Japanese gold shipments to Peru in August and September 1941.
subfiles.summary: The shipments total 818 kilograms; Grew seeks details about consignees and use.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram 1696
subfiles.about: The paraphrase repeats the quantities and vessels involved in gold shipments to Peru.
subfiles.summary: Records shipments of 260 and 558 kilograms and requests further particulars.

subfiles.title: Additional copy of Tokyo telegram 1696
subfiles.about: A further copy reports the same two Japanese gold shipments to Peru.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the August and September shipments and planned follow-up.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Tokyo gold shipment telegrams
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards paraphrases of Tokyo telegrams 1696 and 1726.
subfiles.summary: Transmits reports on Japanese gold shipments to Peru.

subfiles.title: Confidential instruction concerning Japanese gold in Peru
subfiles.about: The instruction seeks comment on reports of Japanese gold bullion arriving in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Relays confidential shipment reports and requests a despatch with comments.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1726 from Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew identifies the consignee and reported purpose of Japanese gold shipments to Peru.
subfiles.summary: The Bank of Japan sent gold through the Yokohama Specie Bank to N. Kobayashi in Lima. Japan said it would pay officials and imports, but Grew's Peruvian source suspects other uses and observes that banking credits were already available.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram 1726
subfiles.about: The paraphrase restates the consignee, stated uses, and doubts about the gold sent to Peru.
subfiles.summary: It identifies N. Kobayashi as the bank's Lima agent and relays a Peruvian diplomat's suspicion that the gold could fund propaganda or other activities. It also notes existing credit arrangements and a shipment of school books.

subfiles.title: Confidential communication to the American ambassador in Lima
subfiles.about: A mostly illegible confidential communication is addressed to the ambassador in Lima.
subfiles.summary: Only its date, confidential marking, and addressee are legible.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese gold in Argentina and Brazil
subfiles.about: The memorandum explains the commercial significance of reported Japanese gold shipments to South America.
subfiles.summary: Japanese gold in Argentina could finance purchases competing with U.S. purchases; a reported Brazil shipment may matter similarly.

subfiles.title: British-source report on Toa Maru bullion
subfiles.about: A report claims the Toa Maru discharged bullion in Buenos Aires and retained more for Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Reports an unverified $3 million discharge and $2 million remaining aboard.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1059 to Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: The Department relays the British-source allegation about Toa Maru bullion.
subfiles.summary: Asks the embassy to investigate alleged bullion destined for Brazil.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1635 from Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.from: Caffery, American Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Caffery reports checks of the Toa Maru cargo in Rio de Janeiro.
subfiles.summary: Officials found no gold but were investigating a heavy box consigned to the Japanese Embassy.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram 1635 for the Navy
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards a paraphrase of Caffery's cargo report.
subfiles.summary: Reports no gold found and notes further inquiry into an embassy consignment.

subfiles.title: Circular telegram on Japanese gold shipments
subfiles.to: Diplomatic missions in Central and South America
subfiles.about: The Department requests urgent reporting on Japanese gold shipments and their purpose.
subfiles.summary: Missions are asked whether shipments pay for goods or establish exchange assets.

subfiles.title: Treasury request for circular telegram
subfiles.about: Treasury requests a cable to American missions about Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Supplies the text later sent as the November 14 circular telegram.

subfiles.title: Undated Asunción telegram 189
subfiles.about: Paraguayan officials report no Japanese gold shipments received or expected.
subfiles.summary: Negative reply to the November 14 circular.

subfiles.title: Dated Asunción telegram 189
subfiles.about: A dated copy repeats Paraguay's negative response.
subfiles.summary: Officials report no shipments received or contemplated.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Asunción telegram
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Asunción's reply about Japanese gold imports.
subfiles.summary: Encloses telegram 189.

subfiles.title: Telegram 616 from Lima
subfiles.about: Peru's Central Reserve Bank confirms two Japanese gold shipments and states their commercial purpose.
subfiles.summary: The second shipment contained 557.7317 kilograms in 38 bars; both shipments paid for goods delivered or to be delivered.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Lima telegram 616
subfiles.about: The paraphrase repeats Peru's account of the two Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Records the second shipment's weight and states that both funded purchases of goods.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Lima telegram
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Lima's response to the gold shipment circular.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a paraphrase of telegram 616.

subfiles.title: Telegram 92 from San Salvador
subfiles.about: The legation reports no Japanese gold shipments to El Salvador.
subfiles.summary: No shipments have arrived or are expected.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of San Salvador telegram 92
subfiles.about: The paraphrase repeats the negative report from El Salvador.
subfiles.summary: No shipments have arrived or are expected.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of San Salvador telegram
subfiles.about: The Department forwards San Salvador's response.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a paraphrase of telegram 92.

subfiles.title: Telegram 333 from La Paz
subfiles.about: Bolivia reports no Japanese gold shipments received so far.
subfiles.summary: Future shipments will be reported.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of La Paz telegram
subfiles.about: The paraphrase repeats Bolivia's negative response.
subfiles.summary: No Japanese gold has arrived; future shipments will be reported.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of La Paz telegram
subfiles.about: The Department forwards La Paz's response to the gold shipment circular.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Bolivian negative report.

subfiles.title: Telegram 178 from Havana
subfiles.about: Treasury and bank sources report no recent Japanese gold imports into Cuba.
subfiles.summary: No Japanese gold imports are known for recent years.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Havana telegram 178
subfiles.about: The paraphrase repeats Cuba's negative report.
subfiles.summary: Treasury and bank officials know of no recent imports.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Havana telegram
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Havana's response.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a paraphrase of telegram 178.

subfiles.title: Telegram 217 from Ciudad Trujillo
subfiles.about: The Dominican Republic reports no recent gold imports from any source.
subfiles.summary: No gold imports are expected soon.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Ciudad Trujillo telegram 217
subfiles.about: The paraphrase repeats the Dominican Republic's negative report.
subfiles.summary: No recent gold imports or imminent arrivals are known.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Ciudad Trujillo telegram
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Ciudad Trujillo's response.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a paraphrase of telegram 217.

subfiles.title: Telegram 560 from Bogotá
subfiles.about: Colombia's Bank of the Republic reports no recent Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Future shipments seem unlikely; the bank will notify the embassy if any occur.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Bogotá telegram 560
subfiles.about: The paraphrase repeats Colombia's report and notes a small unexplained U.S. currency offering.
subfiles.summary: No Japanese gold shipments are known or expected.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Bogotá telegram
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Bogotá's response.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a paraphrase of telegram 560.

subfiles.title: Telegram 256 from Caracas
subfiles.about: The embassy reports no recent Japanese gold shipments to Venezuela.
subfiles.summary: Authoritative sources confirm no recent shipments.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Caracas telegram 256
subfiles.about: The paraphrase repeats Venezuela's negative report.
subfiles.summary: No recent shipments from Japan are known.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Caracas telegram
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Caracas's response.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a paraphrase of the Venezuelan report.

subfiles.summary: “See enclosure 77.”
